title: Choose the visual world for the HackWave web app
question: The roll assigned Registered Post, Acknowledgement Due. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Registered Post, Acknowledgement Due
options.lineage: India Post registered letters and the pink AD card that comes back signed
options.thesis: The page says delivered; only the signed acknowledgement card proves it, and the verifier is the one who signs.
options.viewport: Top nav (New test, Live run, Reports); project and version picker as registered-label rows on the left, the goal and Run test on the right, a sample acknowledgement card showing what a verdict looks like.
options.risk: Postal paper can slide into the warm-cream-plus-red default; the ground stays cool label white and red stays reserved for RED.

raised.raise: No floating cards: every module is hairline-ruled and packed edge to edge, the cure for the floppy layout.
No easing anywhere: the verdict lands as a two-frame stamp, 90 ms, like a postmark hitting paper.
The New test screen shows only the next decision in full; settled ones collapse to one line.
Cost has one fixed ramp: each step's dot grows from rung 1 (saved) to rung 5 (re-plan).
In Reports, picking a step brings that step forward in every version column and quiets the rest.

options.label: Signal Box Mimic Panel
options.lineage: railway signal-box mimic panels and interlocking
options.thesis: Verdicts are signal aspects; the verifier is the interlocking the driver cannot overrule.
options.viewport: The milestone line drawn as track sections that light as the run occupies them, with the verdict lamp at the end lit only by the verifier.
options.risk: The direction already in docs/UI-DESIGN.md and the most familiar one: status-light metaphors are common in CI tools, and dark panels drift toward the neon dashboard default.

options.label: Split-Flap Departure Board
options.thesis: Every run is a row on the board; the verdict column flips when the verifier decides.
options.viewport: Reports as a departure board: one row per version, fixed columns for goal, steps, heals, AI calls and verdict, flaps cascading as results land.
options.case: Strong recognition, every judge has stood under one; loses on clarity, because it shows status but not the page's claim against the store's proof.
options.risk: A black board reads as the dark dev-dashboard default if the type is timid.

options.label: Airport Yellow Wayfinding
options.thesis: Each screen is a junction showing only the choices ahead.
options.viewport: One yellow band per decision: project, version, goal.
options.case: Fuses as a wizard, but judges do not connect signage to proving a test result.
options.kept: Show only the next decision in full; settled choices collapse.
options.risk: Yellow everywhere fights the amber verdict.

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.thesis: Runs as poster rows; the focused one grows.
options.viewport: Rows of run tiles per version.
options.case: Browsing a catalogue is the wrong job for checking a result.
options.kept: One thing in focus; the rest steps back.

options.label: Acetate Manual Tab Board
options.thesis: Sections as coloured divider boards under clear acetate leaves.
options.viewport: A stepped tab rail for New test, Live run, Reports.
options.case: Beautiful system, but too far from the testing story for judges in a few seconds.
options.kept: No easing: every change is a hard two-frame step.
options.risk: Seven section hues compete with four verdict colours.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Steps plotted as stars sized by magnitude.
options.viewport: A run plotted as a constellation.
options.case: Poetic, but a sky chart does not read as a test run.
options.kept: Hierarchy on one fixed size ramp.
options.risk: Navy plus one accent is a known default.

options.label: Japanese High-Density Web
options.lineage: dense Japanese portal and retail sites
options.thesis: Ruled modules packed edge to edge, nothing wasted.
options.case: Right density for an operator, but no story for the core claim.
options.kept: Hairline-ruled modules packed edge to edge; no floating cards.
options.risk: Utility red collides with the RED verdict.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean developer-tool dashboard, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Top bar, a form panel, a run log, a results table with coloured status pills.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other test dashboard by design.
